title: Introduce RAG stub-network toolchain and local playback walkthrough
author: Jordan Reed
description:
Context: Teams repeatedly ask for a compact, reproducible local dev flow that demonstrates RAG tool-calling across a small network of stubbed services (indexer, retriever, tool-runner) and a playback harness for deterministic e2e dev/debug runs.
Motivation: existing quickstarts cover single-process examples and larger orchestrators but lack a lightweight multi-service sandbox that shows tool-chaining failures, retry behavior, telemetry probes, and how Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching/kv-cache hints) change unit economics in dev.
This PR introduces a minimal `rag-stub-network` quickstart plus a docs walkthrough and playback harness.
Summary of changes: 1) quickstart/rig: new `quickstarts/rag-stub-network` with Docker Compose and node/python stubs for indexer, retriever, tool-runner, and a small express shim that proxies Redwood API calls to local model stubs; 2) playback runner: `tools/playback` - a deterministic runner that replays request traces and asserts structured outputs; 3) docs: `docs/quickstarts/rag-stub-network.md` - step-by-step walkthrough, troubleshooting, and telemetry probe guide; 4) examples: `examples/tool-chaining-examples` - three short scenarios (happy path, tool-timeout-retry, partial-index-miss) with sample prompts and expected JSON assertions; 5) telemetry presets: small template to attach debug probes to the quickstart and an example `optimize.toml` with batching/kv-cache suggestions for local testing.
Commits: - "init: add rag-stub-network quickstart scaffold" - adds compose, readme, basic stubs - "playback: deterministic runner and trace format" - adds runner, sample traces, and assertion harness - "docs: add walkthrough + troubleshooting + telemetry probes" - long-form quickstart doc and screenshots/examples - "fix: lint and test fixes after review" - minor code fixes and improved error messages
Changed files (high-level): - quickstarts/rag-stub-network/docker-compose.yml - quickstarts/rag-stub-network/README.md - quickstarts/rag-stub-network/node-retriever/index.js - quickstarts/rag-stub-network/python-tool-runner/worker.py - tools/playback/runner.js - tools/playback/sample-traces/scene-03-tool-timeout.json - examples/tool-chaining-examples/happy-path.json - examples/tool-chaining-examples/timeout-retry.json - docs/quickstarts/rag-stub-network.md - docs/assets/rag-stub-network-diagram.png - scripts/telemetry/presets/rag-stub-debug.json - examples/optimize/optimize.toml
CI notes: - Initial CI run failed lint (eslint/pyflakes) on head commit. - Fixed in commit "fix: lint and test fixes after review"; subsequent CI passed all checks (unit, lint, e2e smoke).
Review conversation summary: - Sofia Nguyen (reviewer): Asked for clearer failure semantics in tool-runner and a compact troubleshooting table in the doc. Jordan: addressed with explicit exit codes and added a troubleshooting section mapping exit codes to mitigation steps. - Carlos Ortega: Requested that the playback runner include a deterministic random-seed option and a smaller sample-trace set to speed CI. Jordan: added `--seed` flag and trimmed CI sample traces to two small scenes. - Maya Li: Noted missing note about Redwood Optimize interactions and suggested an inline example demonstrating how enabling prefix KV caching changes token counts. Jordan: added `examples/optimize/optimize.toml` and an annotated section in the walkthrough. - One thread: minor naming inconsistency between node retriever service (`retriever`) and the docker service name (`retrieve`) discovered and fixed.
Approvals: Sofia Nguyen approved after fixes, Carlos approved after seed/trace adjustments, Maya approved after docs expansion.
Merge: Squash-and-merge on 2025-10-09 after green CI.
Release notes: "Add lightweight RAG stub-network quickstart for local development with deterministic playback runner, telemetry probe presets, and examples demonstrating tool-chaining failure modes and optimize tuning. Ideal for onboarding and debugging tool-calling logic locally."
How to use (short): 1) git clone && cd quickstarts/rag-stub-network 2) docker compose up --build 3) run tools/playback/runner.js --trace examples/tool-chaining-examples/timeout-retry.json --assert to run deterministic scenario 4) follow docs/quickstarts/rag-stub-network.md for troubleshooting and telemetry probe attachment
Rationale and non-goals: - Rationale: lower the engineering friction to reproduce tool-chaining issues, make telemetry-first debugging accessible to product engineers. - Non-goals: not meant to be a production orchestration template or a full-scale autoscaling example.
Follow-ups (tracked in Linear): ENG-3291 add CI smoke to run playback runner nightly; ENG-3302 add a Typescript rewrite option and Windows dev notes.
Notes for maintainers: - Keep the playback trace format stable (v1) and add migration notes if changing fields. - Optimize configuration is intentionally conservative; teams should adapt TTL/batch size to match their real workloads.

merge_outcome: merged via squash into main after green CI
release_notes: Lightweight RAG stub-network quickstart: docker-compose multi-stub dev sandbox, deterministic playback runner, telemetry presets, and optimize example to demonstrate batching/kv-cache effects in local dev.
notes: This quickstart is designed for local debugging and onboarding. It intentionally keeps dependencies small and avoids production orchestration complexity. Please keep the playback runner fast and deterministic; any changes to trace format must include migration notes.
